evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never used the framing 'Great, it looks like we have availability... This will take about 10 to 15 minutes, and you can walk away with a quote you can depend on.' Instead jumped directly into 'are you flexible in your dates?'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked as 'Besides pricing, do we have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call today?' — but only after confirming the date, contact info, and addresses. Probing for the from-address started before this question.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised only one concern: 'I'm just trying to find the pricing... a good in between from all the other companies.' Rep acknowledged with product benefits (no worries coverage, meet your mover, on-time guarantee) but did not ask a follow-up like 'tell me more about what matters most to you when comparing' or probe deeper. One response layer only.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep did not reflect back or summarize what was heard. Moved directly into pitching the three perks without confirming 'So what I'm hearing is...'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (condo), floor (second floor), unit number (133), walking distance/truck access (20–50 feet), special considerations (solid wood dresser, two desks in garage). Also captured three separate move destinations (condo, house, storage unit). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked. No mention of 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. Customer stated 'no boxes,' but rep never offered packing or asked about typical box count. Box-count conversation did not occur.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave only the hourly rate ($192 for two movers + 126 ft truck) and the minimum estimate ($480 for 2.5 hours) for this specific move. Did not anchor to 'typical box count for a home your size' or reference what similar moves usually run. Personalization was minimal — rate tied to truck size 'a bit of overkill for a few pieces' but no broader framing like 'Based on a dresser and two desks with a 25-minute drive, here's what I'd budget.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Fully covered: 'Everything's included in the hourly rate. Fueling, fuel and truck, taxes and insurance, all wrap, all the shing, wrap pads and band protect items being moved, and all tools for disassembling.' Also stated '2.5 hour minimum. Once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.' And: 'We don't have any hidden fee' and 'no deposit to get on our schedule and there are no charges or fees to change the date or cancel the move.' Comprehensive transparency.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any similar check. After stating the $480 estimate, the customer said 'Oh, yeah, no for sure. Okay,' and the rep immediately pivoted to 'Yeah, and then also there is no deposit...' No pause to let the customer sit with the price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Fully delivered early in the call (Section 2): 'We have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in a time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Clear on the discount terms (starts immediately if late).
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Fully delivered in Section 2: 'We have our no worries damage coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate and that provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages and that's on top of the 60¢ per pound coverage that Texas requires.' Covers the $2,000 limit, 'included in our hourly rate' (no add-on), and is presented with no deductible/fine print framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm that the two promises answered the customer's original concerns. The promises were delivered early (Section 2) before the customer raised any specific concern, and no closing loop-back occurred.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked. Rep moved directly to the offer: 'Alright, and then would you like to get on our schedule today or I can go ahead and email all this over...' No version of 'What's still concerning you about this move?' appeared.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all before the ask.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Asked with a built-in out: 'would you like to get on our schedule today or I can go ahead and email all this over, I know you're kind of shopping around.' The 'or I can email this over' is an explicit soft alternative that removes friction. Not a plain ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Yes, mentioned as part of pricing terms: 'There is no deposit to get on our schedule and there are no charges or fees to change the date or cancel the move.' Implies pricing is held if booked.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking was confirmed. Customer chose to email ('If you could email everything that would be greatly appreciated'), and rep agreed to send via email with an invitation to call back or respond to the email to get on the schedule. No date, phone, arrival window, crew size, or crew notes were locked in because no booking occurred.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details across multiple destinations (condo, house, storage) and delivered both the On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage fully and clearly, with transparent pricing framing that included all fees and minimums upfront.
coaching_note: Lead with the quid-pro-quo framing in Section 1 (time-boxed promise + dependable quote) and wait for a yes before probing; ask Their Agenda before collecting logistics; and remove the soft "or I can email this over" from the ask for the business to make it a genuine close.
